chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun from al-Asamm from Mis'ma ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Strike it (the horse) with the heel (using the spur) and do not strike it with the foot."

key_terms.النِّفَارِ: The heel (of the foot), often implying the use of a spur or heel-strike
key_terms.الْعِثَارِ: The foot itself (striking with the sole or toes)
key_terms.اِضْرِبُوهَا: Strike it (imperative, referring to the horse)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between striking a horse with the heel versus the foot according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, distinguishes between 'anif' (a horse that responds to the spur/heel) and 'ithar' (one that requires the foot or whip), offering a nuanced legal criterion for effective equestrian training. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on proportionality and gentleness in animal husbandry, ensuring that discipline is applied only when necessary and with the appropriate tool. This ruling underscores the broader Islamic ethic of treating animals with care, avoiding unnecessary harshness in their training.
